shorts.title: Gin Rummy: probably not the gin you came for

joke.heading:
Probably not
the gin you came for.

shorts.question:
One card
has to go.
shorts.context: Eleven cards. Which one gets the boot?
shorts.questionBottom:
Keep your sets and runs.
Which discard leaves the fewest points?
shorts.selectionContext: The king is outside every set and run.
shorts.selectionBottom:
Keep the three sevens
and both three-card runs.
shorts.answerContext: Only 2♦ is unmatched after your discard.
shorts.answerBottom:
Sets and runs count zero.
Unmatched cards are called deadwood.
shorts.caption: Probably not the gin you came for. No tonic. Just tactics. Which card gets the boot? Discarding K♠ keeps three sevens and both runs, leaving only 2♦ unmatched: two deadwood points. shorts.title: Gin Rummy: hold the tonic

joke.heading:
Gin.
Hold the tonic.
joke.bottom: Two points left. Is that close enough?

shorts.question:
Knock, gin,
or keep playing?
shorts.context: Ten cards remain after your discard.
shorts.questionBottom:
Only 2♦ is unmatched.
Which finish is available?
shorts.selectionContext: Two unmatched points are still two points.
shorts.selectionBottom:
Knock: 10 points or fewer.
Gin: exactly zero.
shorts.answerContext: This hand has 2 deadwood points, not zero.
shorts.answerBottom:
Keep playing is legal, too.
A knock does not guarantee a win.
shorts.caption: Gin. Hold the tonic. Zero deadwood is the recipe, and close enough isn't gin. With two deadwood points after discarding, a knock is allowed, but gin needs zero. Continuing is legal too; this question is about which finish is available, not a promise that knocking will win. Try it yourself: tap our channel, then Get Barbu on Google Play. shorts.title: Gin Rummy: no gin, still a rough finish

joke.heading:
No gin.
Still a rough finish.
joke.bottom:
Compare the deadwood
before you celebrate.

shorts.heading: A knock can lose
shorts.question:
You knocked.
Did you win?
shorts.context: A new deal. Compare the unmatched cards.
shorts.questionBottom:
Every other card is in a meld.
These totals are after any layoffs.
shorts.selectionContext: Your legal knock is not a guaranteed win.
shorts.selectionBottom:
8 is within the knock limit of 10.
But Barbu has only 2 deadwood points.
shorts.answerBottom:
Equal or lower defending deadwood wins.
Classic scoring here: 8 − 2 + 10 = 16.
shorts.caption: No gin. Still a rough finish. You knocked, but you still lost. In this new deal, your unmatched 8♣ is eight deadwood points and Barbu's unmatched 2♥ is two. All other cards form melds and there are no layoffs in this example. The defender's lower deadwood undercuts your knock. With the Classic scoring profile shown here, Barbu earns 8 − 2 + 10 = 16 hand points; other scoring agreements can use a different bonus. Equal defending deadwood also undercuts.
